title: SAST
brief: **Ticket:** add static scanning to the pipeline. Run a scanner and name what it finds.
theory:
## What it is
SAST (Static Application Security Testing) analyses source code **without running
it**, flagging risky patterns and source-to-sink data flows. It is the automated
version of secure code review and runs early in the pipeline.

## How it works
The tool parses your code into an AST/graph and matches rules: Bandit for Python
(flags `shell=True`, `pickle`, `md5`, raw SQL), Semgrep for multi-language
pattern rules. It is fast and shift-left, but produces **false positives**, so
findings need triage.

## In the real world
SAST in CI is table stakes for modern DevSecOps: every pull request gets scanned,
high-severity findings block the merge. Knowing how to run Bandit/Semgrep and
triage their output is a direct, named requirement in AppSec/DevSecOps job posts.

## How to prevent it
(SAST is a detection control.) Wire it into CI, fail the build on high-severity
findings, tune rules to cut false positives, and track findings to resolution so
the same class cannot reappear.
worked_example:
```
$ bandit -r app/
>> Issue: [B602] subprocess with shell=True ... Severity: High
```

knowledge_check.q: A free Python SAST tool is:

investigation.intro: Run a mini scanner to learn the signal, then the real Bandit and Semgrep on the vulnerable app.
steps:
Run the room's mini scanner to see it name the vulnerability class on the `shell=True` line:
```bash
cd /workspaces/examto/rooms/sast
python3 scan.py vulnerable_example.py
```

Now the real tool. Install and run Bandit against the vulnerable app:
```bash
pip install -q bandit
bandit -r /workspaces/examto/appsec-lab/vulnerable_app
```
Bandit flags pickle, subprocess `shell=True`, md5, raw SQL, and urlopen.

Run Semgrep with the repo's ruleset for a second engine's view:
```bash
cd /workspaces/examto
semgrep scan --config appsec-lab/tools/semgrep-rules.yml appsec-lab/vulnerable_app
```
(If Semgrep complains about settings, `export SEMGREP_SETTINGS_FILE=$PWD/.semgrep.yml` first.)
Capture: the vulnerability class the scanner reports on the `shell=True` line (two words).
